query: Tell me about spring travel to Japan's capital
answer_markdown:
Spring in Tokyo, Japan's capital, spans from March through May and is considered one of the most popular times to visit [tokyo-spring-guide::001]. The season is characterized by cherry blossom (sakura) viewing and mild temperatures, typically ranging from 10–20°C (50–68°F) [tokyo-spring-guide::001]. Peak sakura season usually occurs between late March and early April, though exact dates can vary annually based on weather [tokyo-spring-guide::002]. Top hanami (flower viewing) spots include Ueno Park, Shinjuku Gyoen, Chidorigafuchi, and the Meguro River [tokyo-spring-guide::002].

Due to spring being peak season, several booking considerations are important [tokyo-spring-guide::004]. VoyageFlow recommends booking accommodations 3–6 months in advance for travel in late March and early April [tokyo-spring-guide::001]. Hotel rates in central Tokyo can be 30–50% higher during sakura week [tokyo-spring-guide::004]. Flights from North America and Europe often sell out 2–3 months ahead for late-March travel, and popular ryokan (traditional inns) require booking 4–6 months in advance [tokyo-spring-guide::004]. Securing restaurant reservations at high-demand venues before arrival is also advised [tokyo-spring-guide::004]. A typical 5-day spring itinerary might include exploring Shinjuku, visiting Asakusa and Senso-ji Temple, a Sumida River sakura cruise, experiencing Harajuku and Meiji Shrine, a Yoyogi Park hanami picnic, and a day trip to Kamakura or Nikko [tokyo-spring-guide::003].
